value.name: refuse to open envelope in hall
value.description: Asha chooses not to open the envelope in the hallway and instead moves the group to sit down.
evidence: She did not open it in the hall.
She said, "Let's sit down. The dining room, please."

value.name: gather in dining room
value.description: The group goes into the dining room and takes their seats for the reading.
evidence: They went into the dining room and sat.

value.name: Daniel sits at head of table
value.description: Daniel takes the head seat, reflecting his long-standing place in the house.
evidence: Daniel at the head of the table, because no one had told him not to and because he had been sitting there at every meal in this house since he was nine years old.

value.name: Rosa sits at table
value.description: Rosa sits in a chair at the table after Asha gestures for her to do so, marking an unusual but meaningful change in her behavior.
evidence: Rosa to his right, which was not where Rosa would normally have sat — Rosa would normally have been standing somewhere in the kitchen doorway — but Asha gestured to the chair and Rosa sat in it without comment, and Asha thought that the sitting was itself a kind of testimony.

value.name: Marcus takes wall chair with box and camera
value.description: Marcus positions himself by the wall with his banker's box and camera, indicating he is documenting or preserving the proceedings.
evidence: Marcus took a chair by the wall, his banker's box on the floor at his feet, his camera in his lap.

value.name: Asha dons gloves and opens envelope
value.description: Asha puts on cotton gloves and opens the envelope containing the letter.
evidence: Asha put on the cotton gloves again.

value.name: Asha examines letter
value.description: Asha inspects the letter's physical appearance and handwriting before reading it.
evidence: Inside was a single sheet of cream-colored stationery, folded in thirds, written on both sides in a hand that was small and slanted and disciplined, the handwriting of a woman who had been taught penmanship in a Catholic school in San Juan in the late nineteen-forties and had never seen any reason to write any other way.

value.name: Asha rereads letter silently
value.description: Asha reads the letter twice to herself before speaking aloud.

value.name: Asha announces aloud reading
value.description: Asha tells Ms. Serrano she will read the letter aloud and gives her a chance to stop the reading.
evidence: Then she said, "I am going to read this aloud. Ms. Serrano, please tell me if at any point you would prefer me to stop."

value.name: Asha begins reading letter
value.description: Asha starts reading the letter aloud, beginning with an intimate address to her children and Rosa.
evidence: *Mis hijos, y Rosa, who is also mine —*
